 Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Green, Ace Bailey and Mo Bamba will start Sunday’s game against the Spurs. 
 The Jazz won’t have Jaxson Hayes on Sunday, as he exited Friday’s loss to the Rockets with a knee injury. As a result, Bamba moves into the starting lineup and will take on the unenviable task of dealing with Victor Wembanyama. The other change is Green, who replaces Josh Okogie. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaxson Hayes 
 UTA

 Jaxson Hayes (knee) has been ruled out against the Spurs on Sunday. 
 Hayes exited early from Friday’s game against Houston, and he will remain out against San Antonio. Jusuf Nurkić is still out, which means Mo Bamba should start at center, with Kyle Filipowski filling out extra minutes off the bench. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 The Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Okogie, Ace Bailey, and Jaxson Hayes against the Rockets on Friday. 
 The Jazz will start Josh Okogie over Josh Green in this game. Neither of them are fantasy relevant it shouldn’t impact things very much. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Lauri Markkanen (wrist) will be sidelined for at least one month. 
 Markkanen has already missed two games, but it is now being reported that he has a non-displaced fracture in his right hand. It will likely be mid-December before Markkanen suits up again. Josh Green has been filling in as a starter, though it will be Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey that make up the extra usage. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Markkanen is set to miss his second game in a row with a sprained right wrist. It’s the same wrist injury that bothered him earlier this season, so it certainly bares monitoring going forward. Josh Green will likely start again in Markkanen’s absence.

 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Markkanen did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves, so Josh Green moved into the starting lineup. Green should get another start if Markkanen remains out on Tuesday. 
 Josh Green 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Green, Ace Bailey and Jaxson Hayes will start Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 The Jazz are without Lauri Markkanen (wrist) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. As a result, Green will make his second start of the season, after starting in an October 28 loss to the Spurs.

 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Markkanen, who missed a game earlier this season with a sprained right wrist, is back on the injury report for the same reason. Josh Green replaced him in the starting lineup in an October 28 game against the Spurs and could do the same on Sunday if Markkanen can’t play. 
 Mo Bamba 
 UTA 
 Center 
 #44 
 Mo Bamba (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Bamba was listed as questionable with a right ankle sprain, but has since been cleared to play against the Pelicans Wednesday. He’ll have his usual bench role behind Jaxson Hayes. 
 Mo Bamba 
 UTA 
 Center 
 #44 
 Mo Bamba (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Bamba played 18 minutes off the bench in Monday’s loss to the Spurs, tallying eight points, eight rebounds and two blocks. If he can’t play on Wednesday, Kyle Filipowski or Tony Bradley could move into the rotation to back up Jaxson Hayes. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Markkanen sprained his right wrist during Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies and did not play on Wednesday against the Spurs. If he can play on Saturday, Josh Green will likely head to the bench.

 HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto reports that the Hawks are signing Rafael Castro to a two-way contract. 
 After going undrafted this past summer, Castro signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Rockets in late September. Waived on October 1, the former George Washington center signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Lakers on October 9, then was waived eight days later. Given the Hawks’ frontcourt injuries, Castro gives them another option to call on if needed. To open a two-way slot for him, the Hawks are waiving injured guard Keshon Gilbert. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
